title: Autoslicing scheduler for heterogeneous prompt/response lengths with KV warming and slab-aware packing
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Background: We see elevated P99 latency and increased GPU memory fragmentation on hosts running mixed prompt/response workloads (chat-style traffic with short prompts + long model-generated responses). Current continuous-batcher coalesces requests by arrival time and token length buckets which achieves good throughput for homogeneous traffic but suffers in three ways for heterogeneous dialogs: 1) Large responses monopolize slots causing prolonged KV residency and displacing cold prefixes; 2) Small, latency-sensitive prompts are delayed behind long sequences; 3) GPU slab fragmentation increases over time leading to out-of-memory tail events.

Goal: Implement an autoslicing scheduler that slices long response work into managed sub-slices with controlled prefetching of KV pages ("KV warming") and slab-aware packing so that small prompts can be scheduled into reclaimed micro-slots without reloading large KV segments. Target improvements: reduce P99 latency for short prompts by >=25% under mixed load, reduce GPU memory fragmentation incidents by 40%, and preserve or improve aggregate token throughput within 5% of current baseline.

Acceptance criteria:
- Autoslicing enabled in canary pool for runtime-1.20 with feature flag `autoslice_kv_warm`.
- P99(short prompt) reduced by >=25% in 95th percentile of test runs for mixed workload replay (production trace subset).
- Measured GPU slab-entropy metric decreases by >=40% over 72-hour canary compared to baseline.
- No increase in token generation error rate or correctness regressions detected by evals (prompt sets run nightly).

Approach and design notes:
1) Autoslice model: For in-flight long-generation requests, split internal scheduler representation into N micro-slices (N configurable; default 4) such that each micro-slice holds a fixed token budget and an associated KV residency window.
2) KV warming: when scheduling a micro-slice that will require accessing KV segments not resident on GPU, prefetch asynchronously while the micro-slice waits in a short backoff queue. Prefetch budget is bounded by per-GPU KV-budget to avoid exhausting memory.
3) Slab-aware packing: track slab occupancy by "slab tags" (model + kv-segment id + residency age). Scheduler prefers to pack short interactions into slabs with low-residency cost and consolidate long micro-slices onto slabs marked for sustained residency.
4) Reclamation & coalescing heuristics: reclaim micro-slots from paused slices if short prompt has latency urgency score above threshold. Coalesce reclaimed micro-slots when contiguous to reduce kernel launch overhead.
5) Safety: maintain compatibility with existing fallback paths (full-response single-slice) and an emergency OOM bail-out that converts micro-slices back to baseline allocation.

Implementation plan:
- Phase A (prototype): implement micro-slice representation and basic autoslice placement policy; unit tests for slice state transitions. (ENG-31877 as reference for coalescing primitive.)
- Phase B (KV warm): implement prefetch queue and KV budget accounting; integrate with KV cache statistics and eviction hooks.
- Phase C (slab tags): add slab tagging and packing algorithm; offline simulator to validate slab-entropy improvements using recorded traces.
- Phase D (canary + telemetry): roll out behind feature flag; collect P95/P99 latency, slab-entropy, KV hitrate, and token throughput metrics; run A/B test against control.

Notes on trade-offs:
- Aggressive autoslicing reduces latency for short prompts but can slightly increase total kernel launches and CPU scheduling overhead; tune N and micro-slice budget to balance.
- Prefetching improves latency at cost of memory headroom; KV-budget throttles must be conservative on smaller GPU SKUs.
- Slab tagging adds metadata overhead but enables long-term reduction in fragmentation.

P99 latency for short prompts reduced >=25% on mixed workload replay
No regression in token-level correctness or generation error rate
experiments: Offline simulation on recorded 24h production trace (trace-2025-10-30)
Canary run on 6 dedicated GPU hosts with autoslice enabled for 72h
A/B traffic split 10% autoslice vs 90% baseline for 48h post-canary
rollout_plan: Start with internal canary pool (canary-tag: autoslice-kv-warm) -> run 72h telemetry -> open A/B at 10% for 48h -> 50% for 24h if stable -> full rollout per-region. Feature flag has emergency kill switch and automatic revert if OOMs exceed 5x baseline in 1h.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: excessive prefetch causes headroom exhaustion on low-memory GPUs. Mitigation: KV-budget per-GPU and adaptive backoff that reduces prefetch concurrency under high slab-entropy. Risk: micro-slice scheduling increases kernel overhead causing throughput regression. Mitigation: coalesce adjacent micro-slices into batched kernel launches when safe.
